**Review: search ad, Pebblebrook Tea Co.**

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Tea Subscription UK" | Descriptive, not a claim. UK is a market we serve. |
| "Monthly loose leaf tea." | Product fact (loose leaf, monthly subscription). OK. |
| "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time." | Allowlisted, exact wording (subscription terms). |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | Allowlisted, exact wording (shipping policy). |

**Other checks**
- **Superlatives, guarantees, health, green claims, urgency, invented numbers:** none.
- **Banned words and slop:** none. The tone is plain, in line with the brand voice.
- **Disclosure:** none needed. Paid social ads from our own account are marked by the platform, and no "Ad" or "Gifted" label applies to our own search ad.
- **Platform policy:** no health, financial or personal-attribute triggers.
- **Landing page consistency:** the ad makes the pause/cancel and free delivery claims, so the landing page must state both as well. I can't see the page, so please confirm this.
- **Character limits:** none were given, so I haven't enforced any. The headline is 19 characters. The description is about 102, which is over the 90-character limit on Google responsive search ad descriptions. If this is going to Google, trim it, for example by dropping "Monthly loose leaf tea." or shortening the delivery line. Check the final count.
- **Approval:** per policy, Sam needs to sign off before anything public goes out.

Nothing in the copy needs changing.
